 55s ago 04.10 EST Kick-off!
 The penultimate match of the 2026 men’s Rugby League World Cup is under way…
 Share Updated at  04.11 EST 1m ago 04.09 EST As they break, the look in Stephen Crichton’s eye is murderous. What a piece of sporting theatre.
 Share 2m ago 04.08 EST Brian To’o and Tino Fa’asuamaleaui are touching foreheads! Jazz Tevaga is all up in Jack Bostock’s grill. I’ve never seen anything like it.
 Share 4m ago 04.07 EST Australia stand on halfway and Samoa advance until they’re nose to nose with the Kangaroos! This is astonishing!
 View image in fullscreen Junior Paulo performs the Siva Tau. Photograph: Cameron Spencer/Getty Images Share Updated at  04.11 EST 6m ago 04.04 EST And that emotional intensity somehow manages to rise with Samoa’s spine-tingling Siva Tau, instigated by Junior Paulo.
 Share 7m ago 04.03 EST There are tears streaming down the faces of Samoa’s players as they lock arms and sing their national anthem. Ronald Volkman is is in floods, Brian To’o is overcome, it is so emotionally charged.
 Share 10m ago 04.01 EST It also started raining as the sides emerged from the tunnel, so we can add a slippery Steeden to the mix. These are far from ideal playing conditions.
 Share 11m ago 03.59 EST What a sight, hundreds of Samoan flags streaming in the wind as the two teams make their way onto Allianz Stadium. The Pacific Island nations have transformed this competition.
 Share 15m ago 03.56 EST In case you needed reminding, Australia are wearing green with gold trim, Samoa are dripping in blue.
 Share 16m ago 03.55 EST The NRL’s form referee, Adam Gee, is in charge of tonight’s proceedings.
 Share 18m ago 03.53 EST Conditions : The south east of Australia is experiencing an unseasonal cold snap so tonight’s temperature will be around 15C, but made to feel much colder thanks to a serious southerly. We saw last night how much a strong wind can impact a game so both teams will need to be wise to the conditions and adjust accordingly.
 Share 19m ago 03.51 EST For anyone watching this match in Australia, I hope you’ve enjoyed Trent Robinson’s punditry as much as I have. The Roosters coach has been a superb TV analyst, offering intelligent insight delivered matter of factly.
 Share 26m ago 03.45 EST Tonight’s victors will take on New Zealand in next Sunday’s world cup final. The Kiwis look the most accomplished side in the competition and last night downed Tonga with Jahrome Hughes pulling the strings and Kalyn Ponga showing his class just three weeks after fracturing his left arm.
 New Zealand down spirited Tonga to reach Rugby League World Cup final Read more Share 30m ago 03.41 EST The crowd is building for the second match of the day. Earlier Australia’s Jillaroos reached their fifth consecutive World Cup final, but they were pushed hard by Fiji Bulikula.
 Abbi Church powers Australia to win over spirited Fiji as hosts reach Women’s Rugby League World Cup final Read more Share Updated at  03.43 EST 33m ago 03.37 EST Like a US midterm electoral map it is a sea of blue inside Allianz Stadium this evening. It is a sellout and the vast majority of fans are here to cheer on Samoa, not the nominal home team, Australia.
 Share 38m ago 03.32 EST Team News
 Australia : Kevin Walters revealed his hand last weekend so it is no surprise to see Reece Walsh starting ahead of James Tedesco at fullback, and Tom Dearden beating Sam Walker in the race for a starting berth in the halves. Latrell Mitchell and Cameron Murray are fit enough to make the bench, where they will join Ethan Strange, who retains his place after an eye-catching cameo against Cook Islands.
 Samoa: Just one enforced change for Ben Gardiner with Ronald Volkman replacing the injured Chanel Harris-Tavita at five-eighth. The Eel came on for the Warrior against Tonga after the starting No 6 pulled his hamstring kicking for goal.

 Share Updated at  03.31 EST 55m ago 03.15 EST Preamble
 Jonathan Howcroft Hello everybody and welcome to live coverage of Australia v Samoa in the second semi-final of the 2026 men’s Rugby League World Cup . Kick-off at Allianz Stadium in Sydney is from 8.05pm local time (9.05am GMT). 
 The penultimate fixture of a thoroughly entertaining tournament will determine who will start the 2026 men’s rugby league world cup final against New Zealand as underdogs. It would be among the greatest upsets in the sport’s history if Australia are not on the bill to face the Kiwis in Brisbane next weekend but the Kangaroos have yet to hit any kind of form and they will be facing a fiercely motivated foe in Samoa.
 Rugby League World Cup: adversaries gather at Australia’s gate but main threat comes from within | Jack Snape Read more To say Australia’s world cup so far has been underwhelming but would be an understatement. Kevin Walters’ squad and team selection has invited criticism, his forward pack has been well beaten twice, and matches have been won by moments of individual brilliance as opposed to methodical representative football. If the strategy has to been to ease into the contest after a gruelling NRL season then tonight is when the shackles have to be removed.
 Tonga’s gripping win over Samoa a victory for Pasifika pride at Rugby League World Cup Read more Samoa boast a side studded with State of Origin matchwinners, many of whom would command places in the current Australian line-up. And they will have a point to prove after falling narrowly to Tonga last time out in a match where they had enough chances to win.
 They have the power up front to rattle Australia, and the strike out wide to finish them off. The challenge will be whether the spine can control proceedings when the stakes are so high.
 I’ll be back with final team lists and more shortly. Please send me your emails and keep me company throughout the evening. The address is jonathan.howcroft.freelance@theguardian.com .
